rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening poetic examples use alif forms for duals, supporting the dialectal construction under discussion.
rows.anchor: فأطرق إطراق الشجاع ولو يرى … مساغا لناباه

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub says some Banu Asad use alif-form duals even in accusative examples, such as رأيت رجلان and اشتريت ثوبان.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب هؤلاء يقولون : رأيت رجلان واشتريت ثوبان

rows.speaker: رجل من بني ضبة
rows.claim: A pre-Islamic poet from Banu Dabba uses العينانا with alif, while ومنخرين follows the widespread case form and the rest follows that dialect.
rows.anchor: قال رجل من بني ضبة جاهلي : أعرف منها الجيد والعينانا …

rows.speaker: آخر
rows.claim: A cited poem offers further evidence for dual nouns retaining alif in this usage.
rows.anchor: وقال آخر : طاروا علاهن فطر علاها … واشدد بمثنى حقب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take الأخطبان collectively for two male shrikes, leaving صريف ناباه as the relevant dual-alif evidence.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الأخطبان ذكر الصردان ، فصيرهما واحدا فبقي الاستدلال

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says this usage, though rare, is more analogical: fatḥa before the dual marker favors alif, and a following yāʾ would turn to alif.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء وذلك وإن كان قليلا أقيس لأن ما قبل حرف التثنية مفتوح

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub explains the speakers' form as a move toward alif, the lightest of the long vowels.
rows.anchor: وقطرب ذكر أنهم يفعلون ذلك فرارا إلى الألف التي هي أخف حروف المد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls the analogical account the strongest explanation offered for the verse's dual form.
rows.anchor: هذا أقوى الوجوه في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the alif may be integral to the word and therefore immune to inflectional change; if إن هذين is allowed, إن هذان is at least allowable too.
rows.anchor: الألف في هذا من جوهر الكلمة والحرف الذي يكون من جوهر الكلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second response treats إن as affirmative نعم; poetry supports this use, with its final hāʾ as hāʾ al-sakt, as in 69:29.
rows.anchor: الوجه الثاني : في الجواب أن يقال إن ههنا بمعنى نعم

rows.speaker: المعترضون
rows.claim: The objectors say a lām may normally enter the predicate only when إن has entered the subject; otherwise it belongs on the subject.
rows.anchor: واعترضوا عليه فقالوا : اللام لا تدخل في الخبر على الاستحسان

rows.speaker: المجيبون
rows.claim: The reply cites poetic lines with lām on a predicate after an unmarked subject, including أم الحليس لعجوز and خالي لأنت.
rows.anchor: أم الحليس لعجوز شهر به

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub reports both a line with lām after إن opened, which he heard that way, and colloquial examples of lām on a predicate.
rows.anchor: وقال قطرب وسمعنا بعض العرب يقول : أراك المسالمي

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni supplies a poetic example with lām in the predicate of أمسى, and Qutrub reports Arabs saying إني رأيته لشيخا.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني أنشدنا أبو علي : مروا عجالى فقالوا كيف صاحبكم

rows.speaker: المعترضون
rows.claim: The objectors dismiss such examples as rare poetic necessities and say the Qur'an is far above poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: هذه الأشعار من الشواذ وإنما جاءت كذا لضرورة الشعر

rows.speaker: المعترضون
rows.claim: They argue that lām emphasizes the subject's attribution to its predicate, so it belongs on the subject; إن occupies that emphatic position and forces lām onto the predicate.
rows.anchor: اللام تفيد تأكيد موصوفية المبتدأ بالخبر واللام تدل على حالة من حالات المبتدأ

rows.speaker: المعترضون
rows.claim: They distinguish repeated negation, where the second particle reinforces a negation that changes meaning, from a second affirmative emphasis, which would be redundant.
rows.anchor: لكنا قد أدخلنا حرف التأكيد على حرف التأكيد وذلك ممتنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the anti-lām objection: transmitted usage outranks analogy, and weak rationalizations cannot displace clear transmission.
rows.anchor: الكل اتفقوا على أنه إذا اجتمع النقل والقياس فالنقل أولى

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj treats إن as نعم and supplies an understood assertion, نعم هذان لهما ساحران, placing lām on the subject; al-Mubarrad and Ismail ibn Ishaq preferred this analysis.
rows.anchor: قال : إن وقعت موقع نعم واللام في موقعها والتقدير نعم هذان لهما ساحران

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni objects that an omitted subject is permissible only when already obvious; if already known, it needs no emphatic lām.
rows.anchor: الأصل أن المبتدأ إنما يجوز حذفه لو كان أمرا معلوما جليا

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni says ellipsis is concise while emphasis expands speech, so combining subject deletion with emphasis is incoherent and deleting the emphasis would be preferable.
rows.anchor: الحذف من باب الاختصار والتأكيد من باب الإطناب فالجمع بينهما غير جائز

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni invokes Basran rejection of emphatically marking an omitted resumptive pronoun, as in زيد ضربت نفسه.
rows.anchor: امتناع أصحابنا البصريين من تأكيد الضمير المحذوف العائد على المبتدأ

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni says grammarians call أم الحليس لعجوز a poetic necessity; if al-Zajjaj's parse were valid, they would not have done so.
rows.anchor: النحويين حملوا قول الشاعر : أم الحليس لعجوز شهر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi answers that هذان in the wording identifies the omitted subject, while omission of an emphatic element has no such verbal clue; the known subject need not be redundantly emphasized.
rows.anchor: إنما حسن حذف المبتدأ لأن في اللفظ ما يدل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says زيد ضربت نفسه does not prove deleted pronouns cannot be emphasized: نفسه is an object because an expressed noun takes precedence over the pronoun.
rows.anchor: نفسه مفعولا فلا يمكن جعله تأكيدا للضمير فتأكيد المحذوف إنما امتنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls the appeal to earlier grammarians' treatment of the poem a very weak objection; predecessors' failure to notice a parse does not invalidate it.
rows.anchor: ذهول المتقدمين عن هذا الوجه لا يقتضي كونه باطلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third response says إن is weak in government because it resembles a verb, so its subject can retain nominative case.
rows.anchor: الوجه الثالث : في الجواب أن كلمة إن ضعيفة في العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إن resembles verbs in form because it has three letters, ends in fatḥa, and attaches to nouns, and in meaning because it emphasizes a noun's predicate attribution as a verb contributes meaning to a noun.
rows.anchor: أما اللفظ فلأنها تركبت من ثلاثة أحرف وانفتح آخرها ولزمت الأسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since إن resembles verbs, Razi says it should resemble them in government as well.
rows.anchor: أنها لما أشبهت الأفعال وجب أن تشبهها في العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi tests all four possible case patterns: raising both has no effect, lowering both violates verbal government, and raising the subject while lowering the predicate reverses a verb's normal order; thus إن takes an accusative subject and nominative predicate as a derivative operator.
rows.anchor: القسم الرابع : وهو أنها تنصب الاسم وترفع الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because إن's accusative force is incidental, the subject's original mubtada status can still govern nominative; that original, essential status outranks إن's derivative effect, making nominative preferable or at least permissible.
rows.anchor: وصف كونه مبتدأ يقتضي الرفع وحرف إن يقتضي النصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The competing original and derivative case forces explain why a noun conjoined after إن's predicate may be either nominative or accusative.
rows.anchor: إذا جئت بخبر إن ثم عطفت على الاسم إسما آخر جاز فيه الرفع والنصب معا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra derives هذا from ذا plus an added hāʾ, then the dual alif; when identical alifs meet, the dual alif drops, leaving the original alif, which إن cannot govern away.
rows.anchor: الوجه الرابع : في الجواب قال الفراء : هذا أصله ذا زيدت الهاء

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others say the surviving alif, whether original or substituted for the original, counts as essential and cannot be removed by an external governor; this reduces to al-Farra's account.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : الألف الباقي إما ألف الأصل أو ألف التثنية

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj reports an old grammarian analysis with a hidden pronoun of شأن: إنه هذان لساحران.
rows.anchor: حكى الزجاج عن قدماء النحويين أن الهاء ههنا مضمرة والتقدير إنه هذان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With light إن, the following noun is nominative and lām in the predicate is obligatory, distinguishing affirmative إن from negative إن; heavy إن allows the predicate lām optionally.
rows.anchor: فأما من خفف فقرأ إن هذان لساحران فهو حسن فإن ما بعد الخفيفة رفع

rows.speaker: بعض العرب
rows.claim: Some Arabs let light إن govern like full إن, by analogy with deficient كان: semantic force remains even when verbal-form resemblance is lost.
rows.anchor: من العرب من يعمل إن ناقصة كما يعملها تامة اعتبارا بكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usual non-governing light إن shows that heavy إن's verbal-form resemblance is part of the cause of its government; lightening removes that resemblance, unlike كان, a true verb governed by meaning.
rows.anchor: وأما اللغة الظاهرة وهي ترك إعمال إن الخفيفة دالة على أن الشبه اللفظي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The magicians' prostration shows that Moses' staff became a serpent and swallowed their magic; expert magicians recognized the act as outside their craft.
rows.anchor: دلالة على أنه ألقى ما في يمينه وصار حية تلقف ما صنعوا

rows.speaker: رئيسهم
rows.claim: Their chief reportedly argued that their tools remained when they lost ordinary contests; if Moses' feat were magic, where were the objects they had cast?
rows.anchor: ويقال : قال رئيسهم كنا نغالب الناس بالسحر وكانت الآلات تبقى علينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chief's reasoning takes the objects' transformation as evidence for an all-knowing, powerful Creator and the feat on Moses' hand as proof of his true prophethood; the magicians therefore repent, believe, and prostrate in utmost submission.
rows.anchor: فاستدلوا بتغير أحوال الأجسام على الصانع العالم القادر وبظهورها على يد موسى

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash explains أُلقيوا as a figure for speed: they prostrated so quickly that they seemed to be thrown down.
rows.anchor: التأويل فيه ما قال الأخفش وهو أنهم من سرعة ما سجدوا كأنهم ألقوا

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: The Kashshaf contrasts their two acts of casting: they had just thrown ropes and staffs for disbelief, then soon threw down their heads in gratitude and prostration.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : ما أعجب أمرهم قد ألقوا حبالهم وعصيهم

rows.speaker: رُوي
rows.claim: An unattributed report says they did not raise their heads until they saw Paradise, Hell, and the reward of their inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وروى أنهم لم يرفعوا رؤوسهم حتى رأوا الجنة والنار ورأوا ثواب أهلها

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima reports that while prostrating, God showed them the places in Paradise where they would eventually dwell.
rows.anchor: وعن عكرمة : لما خروا سجدا أراهم الله في سجودهم منازلهم

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qadi calls Ikrima's report remote: seeing Paradise directly would compel belief and undermine the voluntary faith expressed in their plea for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : هذا بعيد لأنه تعالى لو أراهم عيانا لصاروا ملجئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi replies that Abraham, despite certainty of forgiveness, still said he hoped God would forgive him; the magicians could similarly speak of hope after a vision.
rows.anchor: لما جاز لإبراهيم عليه السلام مع قطعه بكونه مغفورا له أن يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The public miracle gave all observers clear premises: events need a cause, and humans cannot create huge animals instantaneously and then shrink them, proving a world-governing Creator.
rows.anchor: حدثت أمور فلا بد لها من مؤثر والعلم بذلك ضروري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the deniers knew these premises but chose ignorance; reason alone is insufficient, since God must create premises, awareness of their order, and conclusions in hearts, so all proceeds by divine decree.
rows.anchor: العقل والدليل لا يكفي بل لا بد من مدبر يخلق هذه المقدمات في القلوب

rows.speaker: التعليمية
rows.claim: The Ta'limiyya infer that because the magicians say they believe in the Lord of Aaron and Moses, knowledge of God comes only through the Imam; Razi calls this weak and says their wording has other benefits.
rows.anchor: التعليمية احتجوا بهذه الآية وقالوا : إنهم آمنوا

words: لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their answer to Pharaoh's threat shows full certainty in religious fundamentals: they will not prefer him over clear proofs, since worldly gains and harms cannot rival those of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: بما يدل على حصول اليقين التام والبصيرة الكاملة لهم في أصول الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse supplies an understood repeated على: they will not prefer Pharaoh over the proofs or over obeying and worshipping their Creator.
rows.anchor: التقدير لن نؤثرك يا فرعون على ما جاءنا من البينات وعلى الذي فطرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second parse takes والذي فطرنا as genitive in an oath.
rows.anchor: الوجه الثاني : يجوز أن يكون خفضا على القسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their words do not command Pharaoh to carry out his threat; they declare that it cannot turn them from faith or from practicing the truth they know.
rows.anchor: لا على معنى أنهم أمروه بذلك لكن أظهروا أن ذلك الوعيد لا يزيلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reading has نقضي, 'we spend' this worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( نقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا ) ووجهها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the received reading, الحياة is an accusative of time, extended by treating the adverbial as an object, as in صمت يوم الجمعة صيم.
rows.anchor: الحياة في القراءة المشهورة منتصبة على الظرف فاتسع في الظرف باجرائه مجرى المفعول به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh's judgment reaches only this fleeting worldly life, whereas their aim is lasting afterlife happiness; reason favors enduring finite harm to gain eternal bliss.
rows.anchor: قضاءك وحكمك إنما يكون في هذه الحياة الدنيا وهي كيف كانت فانية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says rulers compelled some subjects to learn magic, then required older practitioners to teach youths, so the magicians were forced both to learn and teach.
rows.anchor: أولا والتعليم ثانيا مكرهين قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says there were seventy-two leading magicians, two Copts and the rest Israelites; they saw Moses' staff guard him while he slept and concluded he was no magician, yet Pharaoh insisted on a contest.
rows.anchor: أن رؤساء السحرة كانوا اثنين وسبعين ، إثنان من القبط ، والباقي من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says magicians were forcibly assembled from the cities to challenge Moses and perhaps compelled to perform magic as well.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : إن السحرة حشروا من المدائن ليعارضوا موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: Amr ibn Ubayd says a ruler's summons is coercion; Razi rejects this because a summons without fear is not compulsion.
rows.anchor: قال عمرو بن عبيد : دعوة السلطان إكراه وهذا ضعيف لأن دعوة السلطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is better in reward for obedience and more enduring in punishment for disobedience, answering Pharaoh's claim about which side has harsher, longer punishment.
rows.anchor: ثوابا لمن أطاعه . { وأبقى } عقابا لمن عصاه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan marvels that former unbelievers gained faith in an instant and accepted persecution, while some who accompany the Qur'an for sixty years later sell their religion cheaply.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : سبحان الله القوم كفار وهم أشد الكافرين كفرا ثبت في قلوبهم الإيمان

words: لَن نُّؤْثِرَكَ عَلَىٰ مَا جَآءَنَا مِنَ ٱلْبَيِّنَٰتِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their speech turns from the threat and their steadfast response to the contrasting fates of believers and criminals at the Resurrection, beginning with the criminal's Hell in 20:74.
rows.anchor: ثم ختموا هذا الكلام بشرح أحوال المؤمنين وأحوال المجرمين في عرصة القيامة
